question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Chebyshev distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{\infty }(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{\infty }
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{\infty }=max(|{v}_{1}|,|{v}_{2}|,…,|{v}_{N}|).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{\infty }(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{\infty } \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 8\end{aligned}]‖}_{\infty } \\  & =max(|1-(-7)|,|-2-8|) \\  & =max(8,10) \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
